_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@2a5029c0d3e6: Early Childhood Development Credit — Residents with Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4) of less than $90,000 who paid qualifying early childhood development expenses (e.g., preschool, child-development books/materials, lesson plans, educational activities) for a dependent aged three through five. Claimed in lieu of (not in addition to) the Child and Dependent Care Credit — only one of the two may be taken per year. For married separate filers the $90,000 limit applies only to the income of the spouse claiming the dependent.
_strings.@@37fe6af9ddae: IA 126 (Iowa Nonresident and Part-Year Resident Credit Schedule), form number 41-126, filed together with the IA 1040. (Iowa does not use a separate nonresident return; nonresidents/part-year residents file the IA 1040 and attach the IA 126.)
_strings.@@4cf945d1e9e4: Credit amounts/limits are not independently verified: State credits were researched from the cited DOR sources and are not tax advice — confirm each amount and your eligibility at the cited source before claiming it.
_strings.@@4d42ad525021: Mailing address: Some state facts could not be independently re-confirmed — see the pack's `unverified` list; confirm at the cited DOR source before relying on a specific figure/address.
_strings.@@782b87d6f398: 2023 IA 1040 Iowa Individual Income Tax Return (form 41-001) - starting lines (Step 4: line 1 Federal total income, line 2 Federal taxable income, line 3 Net Iowa modifications, line 4 Iowa taxable income) and mailing address / check payee
_strings.@@79f1aee7f34c: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Residents with Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4) of less than $90,000 who paid qualifying child/dependent care expenses and qualify for the federal child and dependent care credit (must attach completed federal Form 2441). For married filing jointly, both spouses' Iowa taxable income is combined to test the $90,000 limit. Only one of the Child & Dependent Care Credit OR the Early Childhood Development Credit may be claimed per year. Generally cannot be claimed if filing status is married filing separately.
_strings.@@7ab5b69ed6e3: Tuition and Textbook Credit (K-12) — A parent/taxpayer who claims a dependent attending grades K-12 at an accredited Iowa elementary or secondary school (or receiving qualifying private instruction) and who paid tuition and textbook expenses for that dependent. Only the spouse/parent claiming a given dependent may claim that dependent's expenses; expenses paid with 529-account distributions may qualify.
_strings.@@93b4864e0c9f: Iowa Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — Available only to taxpayers who qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). Iowa simply piggybacks on federal EITC eligibility (earned income, AGI, investment-income, and qualifying-child rules are determined at the federal level). A taxpayer who qualifies for the Iowa low-income exemption may file an Iowa return solely to claim a refund of this credit.
_strings.@@96ce13e635bb: Low-Income Exemption (with elevated threshold for filers age 65+) — This is an exemption from Iowa income tax (not a dollar-amount credit) functioning as Iowa's primary low-income and senior relief on the IA 1040 — Iowa has no separate 'elderly credit' line. A taxpayer is exempt from Iowa income tax if Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4, with required add-backs) is at or below the threshold for their filing status. Senior filers (taxpayer or spouse age 65 or older on 12/31/23) qualify under a substantially higher threshold.
_strings.@@bb55b8da0c75: Treaty conformity — IA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Iowa conforms. Beginning with tax year 2023 the IA 1040 was substantially revised so that "The starting point for taxation on the IA 1040 is now federal taxable income" (2023 IA 1040 Expanded Instructions). The form's Step 4 computes Iowa taxable income as federal taxable income (IA 1040 line 2, from federal 1040 line 15) plus net Iowa modifications from IA 1040 Schedule 1. Iowa applies rolling IRC conformity ("The calculation of Iowa taxable income is the same as the calculation for federal taxable income"). Federally treaty-exempt income is excluded from federal AGI/federal taxable income before it ever reaches the Iowa return, and there is NO treaty/foreign-income re-inclusion among the Schedule 1 additions (Column A additions are limited to items such as interest from state/municipal securities, certain dividends, depreciation/Section 179 nonconformity, and pre-2023 federal NOL carryforward). This is reinforced by Iowa Admin. Code rule 701—300.17, which states a resident is taxed on all income "except when an item of income is specifically exempted from taxation by a provision of federal or Iowa law." Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.

citation.source: Iowa Department of Revenue — 2023 Tax Calculation Worksheet (41-026): NON-JOINT FILERS (filing status 1, 3, 4, or 5) $0-$6,000 at 4.40% (.044), $6,000-$30,000 at 4.82% (.0482) plus $264.00, $30,000-$75,000 at 5.70% (.057) plus $1,420.80, $75,000-and-over at 6.00% (.06) plus $3,985.80; JOINT FILERS (filing status 2) $0-$12,000 at 4.40%, $12,000-$60,000 at 4.82% plus $528.00, $60,000-$150,000 at 5.70% plus $2,841.60, $150,000-and-over at 6.00% plus $7,971.60; worked examples $25,000 -> $1,179.80 (non-joint) and $50,000 -> $2,359.60 (joint). Second pass: 2023 IA 1040 (41-001) Step 4 'Iowa taxable income. Add lines 2 and 3' (line 2 = federal taxable income; line 3 = net Iowa modifications from IA 1040 Schedule 1, line 22) and Step 5 line 5 'Iowa Tax from tax rate schedule or alternate tax', Step 3 $40/$20/$40 exemption CREDITS; 2023 IA 1040 Expanded Instructions line 5 ('Use the Tax Calculation Worksheet (41-026) or the 2023 IA 1040 Tax Calculator'; alternate tax = 6% of income over $13,500/$32,000) — both passes agree.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: IA 1040 (41-001) Step 5, line 5: 'Iowa Tax from tax rate schedule or alternate tax' — computed on IA 1040 line 4 'Iowa taxable income' via the 2023 Tax Calculation Worksheet (41-026) or the 2023 IA 1040 Tax Calculator (line 4 = line 2 federal taxable income + line 3 net Iowa modifications). This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: supply 2023 IA 1040 line 4 'Iowa taxable income' = line 2 federal taxable income (federal 1040, line 15) + line 3 net Iowa modifications (IA 1040 Schedule 1, line 22). The 2023 redesign starts the IA 1040 from FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME, so the federal standard/itemized deduction and QBI deduction are already inside the base — Iowa has no state standard deduction or base personal exemptions, and this op subtracts nothing before the schedule. Two schedules only: the 2023 Tax Calculation Worksheet (41-026) prints one schedule for JOINT filers (Iowa filing status 2) and one for NON-JOINT filers (statuses 1, 3, 4, and 5) — single, married filing separately, and head of household ship the identical non-joint schedule; married_filing_jointly ships the joint schedule. CRITICAL — qualifying surviving spouse: Iowa status 5 (qualifying surviving spouse) is a NON-JOINT filer on the 41-026 worksheet, but this op's status aliasing resolves qualifying-surviving-spouse to the married_filing_jointly schedule, which would UNDERSTATE Iowa tax. For an Iowa QSS filer, pass filing_status='single' (the identical non-joint schedule). Printed worksheet constants are EXACT for 2023: the Column C flat add-ons ($264.00 / $1,420.80 / $3,985.80 non-joint; $528.00 / $2,841.60 / $7,971.60 joint) equal the exact cumulative marginal sums, so this op's marginal math reproduces the worksheet to the cent (worksheet examples: $25,000 non-joint -> $1,179.80; $50,000 joint -> $2,359.60). This op then rounds to whole dollars. Cents vs whole dollars: the IA 1040 is captioned 'Enter Dollars and Cents' and the worksheet computes tax to the cent; whole-dollar rounding is OPTIONAL ('To round, drop amounts under 50 cents and increase amounts from 50 to 99 cents to the next dollar' — a .50 tie rounds UP, matching this op). No tax-table mandate: Iowa retired its tax tables with the 2023 redesign; all filers use the 41-026 worksheet or the online IA 1040 Tax Calculator. Exemption CREDITS, not base exemptions (NOT modeled): IA 1040 Step 3 computes personal credits at $40 (enter 1; 2 if filing status 2 or 4), $20 per 65-or-older or blind condition, and $40 per dependent; the Step 3 total is a CREDIT against tax on line 8 — never a base reduction. exemptions ships empty; pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0. Alternate tax (NOT modeled): all statuses except single may compute an alternate tax — 6% (.06) of the alternate-tax-worksheet income above $13,500 ($32,000 if you or your spouse was 65 or older on 12/31/23) — and enter the SMALLER amount on line 5 (check the Step 5 box); status-3 spouses prorate it. Single taxpayers may instead qualify for the Iowa Income Tax Reduction Worksheet. Check these when income is just above the threshold. Low-income exemption (NOT modeled): filers whose Iowa taxable income plus specified add-backs is at or below $9,000 (single/married filing separately; $24,000 if 65+), or $13,500 (all other statuses; $32,000 if 65+), owe no Iowa income tax (check the box between Steps 4 and 5); a dependent filer's threshold is $5,000. Not modeled — later lines: Iowa lump-sum tax (line 6), the Step 3 exemption credits (line 8), tuition and textbook credit (line 9), volunteer firefighter/EMS/reserve peace officer credit (line 10), the IA 126 nonresident/part-year credit (line 13), out-of-state tax credit (line 15), SCHOOL DISTRICT SURTAX and EMS surtax (Step 6 — a local percentage of the line 16 balance), the 15%-of-federal Iowa EITC (line 25), and the child and dependent care / early childhood development credits (line 24). Rate provenance: 2022 Iowa Acts (HF 2317) consolidated the 2023 schedule to four brackets by status as printed on the 2023 41-026 worksheet; the pre-2023 nine-bracket schedule and the net-income starting point are GONE — do not carry pre-2023 figures forward.
